sketches.title: After-Hours Food Chain
sketches.premise: The zoo is locked, the lights are out, and the animals are arguing over who gets to be dinner. On each turn, name a living zoo creature that defeats the creature just named by hunting, eating, trapping, poisoning, or clearly overpowering it.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that your animal directly defeats the standing animal in a plain food-chain or predator-prey way; hiding, fleeing, merely surviving, a larger version of the same animal, or a distant relative does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Say: “I am a [animal]; I [specific attack] the [standing animal].” Example: “I am a crocodile; I clamp down on the zebra’s leg.”
sketches.first_card: I am a mouse; I sneak beneath the sleeping lion’s paw and bite its nose.

sketches.title: Keeper Lockup
sketches.premise: The keepers have vanished, and every enclosure is trying to escape before dawn. Each turn names one zoo object, animal behavior, or simple tool that defeats the last obstacle by locking it, cutting it, blocking it, or forcing it open.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new thing actively stops or defeats the standing thing’s function; going around it, waiting it out, merely being tougher, or using a bigger copy of it loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say: “I am a [thing]; I [action] the [standing thing].” Example: “I am a key; I turn inside the lock and open it.”
sketches.first_card: I am a padlock; I snap shut on the gate and keep every clever little escape artist inside.

sketches.title: Nocturnal Nonsense
sketches.premise: After closing, the zoo’s night shift gets weird: each new animal must defeat the last one with a natural trick it really has. Wings beat walls, venom beats fur, and echolocation beats darkness—but the host will call bullshit on lazy biology.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the newcomer’s real body or behavior directly defeats the standing animal or its useful ability; dodging, outlasting, being a bigger copy, or claiming a vague superpower does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Say: “I am a [animal], and my [real trait] defeats the [standing animal] by [clear effect].” Example: “I am a bat; my echolocation finds the owl even in pitch-black.”
sketches.first_card: I am a skunk; I spray the fox until its grand midnight ambush becomes a crying lesson.

sketches.title: Exhibit A: The Animal Court
sketches.premise: The zoo animals are putting one another on trial for crimes against snack time, dignity, and the furniture. Each turn introduces a courtroom role, object, or rule that defeats the thing before it by proving it, exposing it, silencing it, or sentencing it.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new courtroom element directly undermines the standing claim or role; changing the subject, escaping judgment, repeating a stronger version, or using a merely related legal word loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say: “I am the [court thing]; I [court action] the [standing thing].” Example: “I am a witness; I saw the parrot steal the keeper’s keys.”
sketches.first_card: I am the judge’s gavel; I bang once and shut down the baboon’s entire cross-examination circus.

sketches.title: Zoo Utility Belt
sketches.premise: The animals have raided the lost-and-found and are solving problems with ordinary stuff: rope, soap, umbrellas, buckets, and whatever else the night guard dropped. Each turn names a thing that directly defeats the previous thing’s use.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new object plainly stops, removes, breaks, or reverses what the standing object does; merely avoiding it, enduring it, or offering a larger copy or close cousin fails.
sketches.move_shape: Say: “I am a [ordinary object]; I use [action] to defeat the [standing object].” Example: “I am soap; I dissolve the grease on the slippery ramp.”
sketches.first_card: I am a bucket; I smother the fire before it turns the gift shop into premium charcoal.

sketches.title: Dawn-Shift Roast
sketches.premise: The animals are competing to invent the one insult that makes the previous animal lose its zoo job. Each turn names a different animal and a concrete, funny reason it exposes or defeats the last animal’s supposed advantage.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new animal’s real trait or behavior directly undercuts the standing animal; a generic insult, a dodge, survival, a bigger copy, or a same-family substitute gets laughed off the stage.
sketches.move_shape: Say: “I am a [animal], and I defeat the [standing animal] because [specific real weakness or counter].” Example: “I am a parrot; I repeat the guard’s whistle and make the watchdog chase the wrong alarm.”
sketches.first_card: I am a tortoise; I beat the rabbit because I do not need a nap, a pep talk, or a personality transplant to reach the finish.
